title: OSHA Aerial Lift Checklist (29 CFR 1926.453)
subtitle: Use before each day's work and whenever the lift is set up, used or moved for travel.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item is marked Defect, stop the work or keep the lift out of service until it is corrected, and record what was done.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Setup, controls and loads
items: Lift controls tested today before use and found in safe working condition
The person operating the lift is an authorized person
Personnel-carrier boom platform has platform (upper) controls in or beside the platform within the operator's easy reach, plus lower controls
Lower controls can override the upper controls
Every control is plainly marked with its function
Brakes set before the lift is used
Where outriggers are used, each one rests on a pad or a solid surface
On an incline, wheel chocks are in place before use where they can be safely installed
Workers, tools and materials in the basket and on the boom are within the manufacturer's stated load limits
Insulated portion shows no alteration that might reduce its insulating value; any field modification has written certification from the manufacturer or an equivalent entity

sections.title: Workers in the basket
items: Each worker wears a body belt with a lanyard connected to boom or basket; a body belt is used only for tethering or restraint, not as part of a personal fall arrest system
No tying off outside the lift
No lanyard is attached to an adjacent pole, structure or piece of equipment
Workers keep both feet on the basket floor and nobody sits or climbs on the basket edge
No planks, ladders or other devices used to stand on inside the basket
Nobody working from the lift is wearing climbers
Ground-level controls are operated only with permission from the employee in the lift, or in an emergency

sections.title: Moving and travel
items: No travel with raised boom and occupied basket
Truck is not driven while the boom is elevated in a working position with workers aboard, unless the equipment is specifically designed for that operation
Boom(s) inspected and properly cradled before the lift is moved for travel
Outriggers are in the stowed position before travel
Aerial ladder secured in the lower traveling position by the locking device on top of the truck cab before highway travel
Manually operated device at the base of the aerial ladder engaged before highway travel

references: 29 CFR 1926.453: Aerial lifts (Part 1926 Subpart L, Scaffolds)
29 CFR 1926.502(d) and (e): body belt use, referenced in the note to 1926.453(b)(2)(v)
